RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Reese Carter
Member ID: W769161738
Reference Number: POC-9992A0803A-86478
Date of Notice: 2026-08-17
Service at issue: CPT 63030 — Lumbar laminotomy/discectomy with decompression of nerve root
Requesting/treating surgeon: [Dr. Reyes], MD, Orthopedic Surgery — NPI [not in records]

Dear Appeals Review Committee,

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030 described in the above-referenced Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination. This appeal is being submitted within the 180-day window stated in the notice (received 2026-08-17; deadline 2027-02-13).

**1. The stated reason for denial**

The notice states only that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." The notice does not identify which specific medical policy, clinical guideline, or criteria set was applied, nor does it specify which documentation elements were considered missing. I am unable to fully rebut a criterion-by-criterion determination that has not been disclosed to me, and I have not been given text from Molina's own applicable medical policy to quote here — none was provided in the denial notice, and I could not independently locate a Molina-published policy specific to this CPT code and this plan. I am therefore formally requesting, under my appeal rights, that Molina identify and produce in writing the specific internal rule, guideline, or protocol relied upon in this denial, consistent with the plan's own statement (in its Prior Authorization/Pre-Service Review materials) that "Providers and members can request a copy of the criteria used to review requests for medical services."

**2. The documentation that was, or should have been, part of this request**

The following records were part of, or are being submitted with, this appeal to address any documentation gap:

- **Duration and nature of symptoms:** 18 months of progressive lower back pain, unrelieved by rest, with radicular pain radiating into the right calf.
- **Conservative treatment:** Supervised physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility training, over 10 weeks (2026-04-24 through 2026-07-03), with 18 visits completed, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication trial:** NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief.
- **Interventional treatment:** Corticosteroid (epidural) injection on 2026-05-07, yielding only approximately 3 weeks of partial relief.
- **Imaging:** MRI of the lumbar spine dated 2026-06-23 showing an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing right L5 nerve root.
- **Functional limitation:** Patient is unable to stand more than 10 minutes at a time due to pain.
- **Physical examination:** Positive provocative testing on the affected (right) side, with a neurologic deficit corresponding to the level of nerve root compression seen on imaging.
- **Absence of contraindications:** No active infection, no untreated substance use disorder, BMI 29, non-smoker.

**3. Why this documentation supports medical necessity**

I am not able to quote Molina's own medical-necessity criteria for CPT 63030 because that document was not identified or produced in the denial notice, and I want to be explicit that the plan has not been quoted here. However, I note for the reviewer's benefit that publicly available musculoskeletal-surgery review criteria used elsewhere in the Molina/Evolent utilization-management network for lumbar discectomy and lumbar decompression procedures set out indications such as: primary radicular symptoms that significantly hinder daily activities; failure of a defined trial of conservative treatment; and imaging showing disc herniation or stenosis that correlates with the individual's symptoms and signs. In one such document (Evolent Clinical Guideline 1766, "Lumbar Spine Surgery," a guideline used in some Molina-affiliated markets, though I have not been able to confirm it is the specific criteria set applied to this claim), the surgical indications for lumbar discectomy/microdiscectomy are described as being met "When ALL of the following are present: Primary radicular symptoms noted upon clinical exam that significantly hinders daily activities... Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months... Imaging studies showing evidence of inter-vertebral disc herniation that correlate exactly with the individual's symptoms/signs." The same document describes the lumbar decompression indications as met "When ALL of the following are present: Neurogenic claudication, and/or radicular leg pain that impairs daily activities... Failure of conservative treatment*... Imaging studies demonstrating moderate to severe stenosis consistent with clinical signs/symptoms." I offer this only as an illustration of a widely used, industry-standard benchmark for this procedure family, because Molina's own criteria were not disclosed to me — not as a representation that this is definitively the document Molina applied to this member.

Measured against that kind of framework, the record shows: (a) documented radicular symptoms (right calf radiation, positive provocative testing, corresponding neurologic deficit) that significantly impair daily activities (inability to stand more than 10 minutes); (b) a completed conservative treatment trial well in excess of six weeks — 10 weeks of supervised physical therapy (18 visits), 4 months of NSAIDs, and an epidural steroid injection — all within the last six months, with inadequate or only transient benefit; and (c) an MRI dated 2026-06-23 that correlates precisely with the clinical findings, showing an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis compressing the traversing L5 nerve root, the same nerve root level implicated on exam.

**4. Requested action**

I ask that Molina Healthcare:
1. Reverse the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 63030 for Reese Carter; or
2. If any specific documentation element is still considered missing, identify that element in writing so it can be promptly supplied; and
3. Provide, as requested above, a copy of the specific medical policy or clinical criteria document (title, policy/guideline number, and version/effective date) that was actually used to review this request, as Molina's own materials state members and providers are entitled to receive.

Please notify both me and Dr. [Reyes]'s office of the outcome of this appeal. If additional records are needed, please contact [Dr. Reyes]'s office at [phone number/fax not in records] or me directly at [phone number not in records].

Thank you for your prompt reconsideration.

Sincerely,
